info.title: Ninja Kilat WMS
info.description: Warehouse management for Ninja Van's GrabMart Kilat fulfilment: inbound and putaway, guided picking, weekly stock opname, barcode and license-plate registration, and an isolated training mode.

get.summary: Readiness probe — reports liveness and database connectivity
get.description:
Readiness probe.

Reports database state without failing on it: a database blip should show up
in the payload, not take the pod out of rotation on its own.

get.summary: Who the signed-in user is, their role, and the sites they may work at
get.description: The frontend asks "who am I?" here — the browser never sees the SSO headers.

post.summary: Onboard a new brand and set its default identity mode

get.summary: Search a brand's SKUs by name or code

post.summary: Create one SKU under a brand
Bulk-import a brand's SKUs from CSV — preview by default, commit on request
post.description:
Bulk import from CSV. Preview by default; pass commit=true to apply.

Column names are matched loosely rather than pinned to one file's exact
shape — the Wardah source is an OCR artefact with a trailing formula row and
no stable SKU-code column, and hard-coding it would contradict G5 (onboarding
a brand should be configuration, not code).

get.summary: Live check while a staffer bulk-scans under one locked SKU
get.description:
Live check while a staffer bulk-scans under one locked SKU.

A repeated scan of the same barcode is the normal case — a carton of 40
identical units — so it is 'already registered', not an error (M1.3.4).

post.summary: Bind a batch of scanned barcodes to one pre-selected SKU
post.description:
Bind a batch of scanned barcodes to one pre-selected SKU.

A barcode may resolve to exactly one SKU — enforced by the unique index, not
only by this check (M1.3.7).

delete.summary: Unbinding DELETEs the row and writes the audit trail (PRD §11)
delete.description: Unbinding DELETEs the row and writes the audit trail (PRD §11).

post.summary: Register a new station, hub, or training site
Build the standard layout in one action, so opening station 8 takes a
post.description:
Build the standard layout in one action, so opening station 8 takes a
minute rather than an afternoon (M2.1.5).

get.summary: The one dense screen in the product: the whole station at a glance
get.description: The one dense screen in the product: the whole station at a glance.

get.summary: Recommend a basket size and a free location
get.description:
Recommend a basket size and a free location.

Slotting rules (PRD §7.3): fast movers to levels 2-3, slow movers to level 5
which sits at ~2.0 m and needs a step stool.

post.summary: Give a SKU its basket at a site — one SKU per basket, one basket per SKU
post.description:
Bind a SKU to a basket. One SKU per basket, one slot per SKU per site —
both enforced by unique constraint, not only by this check (M2.2.2).

post.summary: Moving a SKU is an explicit action that writes movements, not an edit
post.description:
Moving a SKU is an explicit action that writes movements, not an edit
(M2.2.3). Stock follows the SKU to the new basket.

get.summary: Resolve any scanned code to either a SKU (Mode A) or one physical unit (Mode B)

post.summary: Open an inbound receipt against a brand delivery or a hub transfer
Scan a unit into a receipt and be told which basket it goes in
post.description:
The receiving scan loop — the core interaction, tuned for the burst.

Never dead-ends: an unknown barcode or a SKU with no basket both return an
outcome the UI can offer a way out of, rather than an error (M3.3.4/5).

post.summary: Close a receipt and start the 24-hour discrepancy clock

get.summary: What a receipt took in, with expected-versus-received variance

post.summary: Mint a block of sequential, unbound plates and materialise them
post.description:
Mint a block of sequential, unbound plates and materialise them.

A plate exists from the moment it is issued: issuing 5,000 creates 5,000
rows, so a scan of any of them is a known object rather than a guess.

get.summary: How many unbound license plates a site has left

post.summary: Bind a freshly-applied license plate to a SKU and put the unit away in one action
post.description:
Apply-then-scan. Binding and putaway are one action, never two (M1.4.2.8).

The staffer sticks a label on the item and scans it; the scan resolves the
SKU, the SKU resolves the basket, and the screen shows where to put it. The
same unit is never scanned twice.

post.summary: Release a license plate so the label can be peeled and reused
post.description: Undo — peel the label and rebind it cleanly (M1.4.2.6).

get.summary: Where one license-plated unit is, and its history

post.summary: The POS creates an order here
post.description:
The POS creates an order here. The dummy generator uses the same endpoint,
so switching to live Hiryu is configuration rather than a rewrite (§9.3).

Deliberately unauthenticated at the user level — this is a machine-to-machine
call. Once §9.1 is settled it is gated by POS_SHARED_SECRET.

get.summary: Pick tasks waiting at a station

post.summary: A claimed task is invisible to other pickers (M5.2.2)
post.description:
A claimed task is invisible to other pickers (M5.2.2).

The conditional UPDATE is the lock: two pickers racing for the same task,
exactly one wins, decided by the database rather than by timing.

post.summary: Confirm a pick by scanning — blocks the wrong shade before it reaches the bag
post.description:
The shade-confusion gate. Shade 07 versus 08 is caught here and nowhere else.

A wrong scan is blocking, with no staff-level override — an override that
exists gets used, and then the gate has no value (M5.2.5, and E13 in §15).

post.summary: Finish a pick task and hand the order to the packing station
Create a stock-count plan over a site's baskets

get.summary: A count plan's progress, and every basket in it

post.summary: Claim a basket to count it
post.description:
Claim a basket to count it.

The UNIQUE(plan_id, basket_id) index is the claim: two staff racing for the
same basket, exactly one wins, and the loser is told who holds it. This is
the direct answer to concurrent staff on one station (M6.2.2).

The expected quantity is deliberately NOT returned. Showing it invites
confirming the number instead of counting it (M6.2.3).

post.summary: Scan a unit into the count
post.description:
Scan a unit into the count.

A foreign SKU is recorded, not rejected — finding the wrong product in a
basket is a real and common outcome, and a system that refuses to hear it
just loses the information (M6.2.5).

post.summary: Reveal expected vs counted
post.description:
Reveal expected vs counted — and only now.

NOTE (flagged in review): prompting for a recount AFTER showing the expected
number defeats the blind count. The recount prompt is returned as a flag and
the client should ask before revealing. Left as-is pending a decision on the
interaction; see §15 E19.

get.summary: Sorted by rupiah value, so a supervisor triages the top of the list rather
get.description:
Sorted by rupiah value, so a supervisor triages the top of the list rather
than reading all 118 rows (M6.3.2).

post.summary: Counting never moves stock by itself
post.description:
Counting never moves stock by itself. A supervisor reviews and approves,
and only then does the ledger change (M6.3.3).

get.summary: On-hand stock at a site, by SKU and location
Scan or type anything and be told where it is
get.description:
Scan or type anything and be told where it is. After the guided flows,
the most-used screen in the product (M7.2).

get.summary: Feeds replenishment (M4.6)
get.description: Feeds replenishment (M4.6) — it suggests, a human decides.

get.summary: The append-only stock ledger — what moved, when, and who moved it
get.description: The immutable ledger. Answers 'where did this stock go'.

Load a named fixture, and print what it created — so a trainer knows what

post.summary: Test orders, through the same endpoint the real POS will use
post.description:
Test orders, through the same endpoint the real POS will use.

Training sites only. An earlier draft allowed this against any site, which
would have had a test order consume real stock and push a wrong number to
Grab (PRD §9.3.4).

ScanResolved.title: ScanResolved
ScanResolved.description:
One endpoint for both identity modes.

The caller scans and the server decides what it was looking at, so the
client never has to know whether a brand is barcoded (PRD §5.1).
